title: Token-phase weighted priority scheduler for fair latency/throughput tradeoffs
creator: Lina Chen
description: Design and implement a token-phase weighted priority scheduler that splits requests into explicit prefill and decode micro-phases and assigns dynamic weights to each request based on latency SLOs, queue aging, and batch efficiency. Unlike the current coarse fairshare or phase-aware schedulers, this approach will allow per-request weight adjustments at phase boundaries and introduce a tunable decay factor to balance tail latency vs aggregate throughput. The ticket covers design, simulation, runtime integration (scheduler module + metrics), A/B benchmarking, and rollout plan with canary settings.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements explicit phase split hooks (prefill -> decode) and exposes per-request weight adjustments at phase boundaries
End-to-end latency P95 for tier-1 routes does not regress more than 5% in canary under production-like load
Throughput (tokens/sec) improves or is neutral compared to the existing phase-aware scheduler for synthetic mixed workloads
New metrics emitted: phase_weight, effective_priority, queue_age_seconds; dashboards updated
Documentation (runtime scheduling guide) and migration notes are published
comments: 2025-11-18 - Lina Chen: Triage - this originated from repeated tail-latency incidents on mixed prefill/decode workloads; initial goal is to reduce age-based starvation without sacrificing batch efficiency.

2025-11-20 - Ravi Patel: Design kickoff; sketched weighted-decay formula: effective_weight = base_priority * (1 + alpha * queue_age) * phase_multiplier. Need simulation to tune alpha and phase_multiplier ranges.

2025-11-24 - Design review (Marco Diaz): Reviewed trade-offs between per-token vs per-request weighting. Recommendation: keep weights per-request at phase boundaries to avoid per-token overhead in hot loops. Added note to consider kernel selection signals (long sequence lengths should favor decode-priority).

2025-11-27 - Engineering notes: Implemented discrete-event simulator to model mixed traffic (short chat turns, long-context completions, embedding requests). Simulator repo: github.com/redwood-inference/simulators/pull/42. Early results show 15-22% P95 reduction for aged short requests when alpha in [0.08,0.14].
2025-11-30 - PR opened: runtime scheduler implementation draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289. Includes new metrics and a feature flag (scheduler.phase_weighted=true).

2025-12-02 - QA feedback (Aisha Khan): Found a regression when phase_multiplier > 2.0 that causes overscheduling of decodes on GPU pools with limited KV cache capacity. Action: add guardrail to cap effective_weight based on current pool utilization.
2025-12-03 - Ravi Patel: Addressed QA feedback; implemented utilization cap and added unit tests for weight capping. Ready for performance benchmarking in canary cluster.
implementation_notes: Integrate phase hooks into request lifecycle: mark boundary after prefill is complete and before decode begins
Expose config knobs via runtime config: alpha (age sensitivity), phase_multiplier_prefill, phase_multiplier_decode, max_effective_weight
Make scheduler decisions soft by assigning a 'priority hint' used by batch builder to influence token slicing rather than hard preemption
Ensure minimal hot-path overhead: compute weight only at phase transition and cache value on request context
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-prioritizing aged requests reduces batching efficiency -> Mitigation: decay alpha during high utilization and use batch efficiency indicator to lower phase_multiplier
Risk: Interactions with kernel selection (large-seq requests) could favor wrong variant -> Mitigation: feed kernel_selection_score into final weight calc as a multiplier
Risk: New metrics and flags increase observability surface -> Mitigation: document and add dashboards and alerts before rollout
next_steps: Run canary A/B with 10% traffic using runtime-1.20 in canary cluster (owner: Ravi)
Collect 72h of P95/P99 and throughput metrics and compare against control (dashboard link attached)
If stable, roll to 50% with automated rollback if P99 tail increases by >10%
Write migration notes and update public runtime scheduling guide
